lxc_aa422cb00489ecc3.text: First meetings often move from basic personal facts to interests and safe everyday topics.

lxc_85e93f1b397c7ef8.text: Names and greetings can also work differently in Japan, France, and Mexico.

lxc_60acc90016d1217f.text: MATCHA shows how people introduce themselves at a first meeting by giving a name, where they come from, their work or school, and a hobby.

lxc_9095ea8427b8de91.text: A simple first meeting often has three layers: identity, interests, and easy connection.

lxc_b68e57040e0a51e4.text: Identity includes a name, a place, and work or school.

lxc_d71302b3a27d0264.text: In Japan, a self-introduction is called jikoshoukai.

lxc_e395951e3a5c52f6.text: A basic order begins with hajimemashite, a first-meeting greeting.

lxc_2115405ba741effe.text: The person then gives a name, where they come from, and their occupation.

lxc_ec1f32a8a9f6970e.text: MATCHA uses Tanaka Miki as an example and includes student, company employee, and designer as occupations.

lxc_c8eb81ec266cf862.text: The introduction can end with the polite close yoroshiku onegaishimasu.

lxc_9901db5ffe4b6da5.text: Name order is important because it can change with the situation.

lxc_5c95669434af0985.text: In Japan today, people usually say the surname before the given name.

lxc_9ca5aeac945e59ac.text: In Yamada Tarō, Yamada is the family name.

lxc_8d8bd6a9941a6b44.text: Yamada Tarō is also a common placeholder man’s name, like John Smith in English.

lxc_bbb6b1eddc3b44e0.text: Yamada Hanako is the matching placeholder woman’s name, like Jane Smith.

lxc_dc8f3ffd77f455a0.text: In English, modern Japanese names have often appeared with the family name last.

lxc_7bed814dc7ae3ca6.text: However, JICE has used family-name-first order in its English documents since January 1, 2020.

lxc_7f51158615cfffc7.text: After identity, interests can help people find an easy connection.

lxc_ba8dbd2a5d2b0585.text: MATCHA says that at school, mentioning hobbies or interests after an occupation can help classmates know someone more quickly.

lxc_8496a82175575430.text: Its example uses shumi, meaning hobby, and gives playing soccer as the hobby.

lxc_8f981d4c4ad9291d.text: People can also share simple likes.

lxc_5c2f2e6ba28ec050.text: The page gives “I like sushi” and a stronger example about liking anime very much.

lxc_9f9fc54bfb5eab7b.text: These small facts show what a person enjoys without giving private information.

lxc_4f1df82688d669f4.text: Talking about hobbies can therefore move a meeting from basic facts toward friendly conversation.

lxc_fba75fe6b1adfba1.text: People do not greet one another in exactly the same way everywhere.

lxc_b6ff099150bcb05b.text: In France, a cheek-kiss greeting is called faire la bise.

lxc_25e1d23cfbc51f4f.text: It can be used among relatives or friends, but this does not mean that every first meeting includes a kiss.

lxc_7bfeecb26ef4c241.text: The custom also changes across the country.

lxc_fb9b8cb853000628.text: A popular French joke says that the city can be known by the number of cheek kisses because the number varies.

lxc_45e5a4b1d5f12eda.text: Faire la bise is very common in southern France, even between male relatives or friends.

lxc_70ce9d423ab57257.text: In the north, it is less usual between unrelated men.

lxc_34d81655957b48cc.text: In Mexico, a title can be an important part of a respectful greeting.

lxc_defde12717ce19d8.text: Titles are used with acquaintances, teachers, neighbors, shopkeepers, and people on the street.

lxc_db5e22dfea632308.text: Na’atik explains that Don plus a first name can respectfully address an older man when his profession is unknown or he is not a professional.

lxc_ef031f008d1d5c92.text: For example, Manuel Gonzalez can be greeted as Don Manuel.

lxc_323d7d576af74749.text: Teachers may greet each other as maestro or maestra without a name.

lxc_0901756df5584b7d.text: These examples show that a first meeting may communicate respect through a title, not only through a plain first name.

lxc_e9c89a9006491a4d.text: After names and interests, people often move into small talk about everyday life.

lxc_eb945b1c625edd1c.text: Small talk is polite conversation about small, safe subjects.

lxc_08f3d2486f57ad3b.text: It usually has a greeting, some conversation, and a closing.

lxc_dc95e33105eb62bf.text: Its purpose is to build or keep a relationship, not to exchange important information.

lxc_a7bc2a04c9e703a4.text: In English-speaking settings, common safe topics include the weather, sports, and television.

lxc_b87133c04abe7778.text: usually receives a short, general answer rather than a detailed personal story.

lxc_d1503590f6bd2248.text: This final layer creates an easy connection while keeping private matters out of a new conversation.
